name: Setting a Contingency Budget for Room Additions in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: How can I build a contingency budget for a Los Angeles County room addition based on my home’s age and site conditions?
mainEntity.text: How can I build a contingency budget for a Los Angeles County room addition based on my home’s age and site conditions?

acceptedAnswer.text: A smart contingency budget for a room addition in Los Angeles County depends heavily on your home’s age and site complexity. For relatively new homes on flat lots with good access, a 10% contingency on construction costs may be adequate. For older homes, especially pre-1970s, homes with prior unpermitted work, hillsides, or tight urban sites, consider 15–20% or more. Start by discussing risk factors with your contractor. Ask what they typically discover behind walls in homes from your era: outdated wiring, undersized framing, deteriorated plumbing, or missing footings. Request a list of “likely surprises” with approximate cost ranges, like $2,000–$5,000 for electrical upgrades or $3,000–$8,000 for structural fixes. Include potential city-driven changes in your contingency, such as extra engineering, revisions requested during plan-check, or added inspection requirements. Site conditions—poor access, limited staging space, or tricky soil—can also drive up labor and equipment costs. Keep your contingency funds separate from your core budget so you do not spend them on optional upgrades early in the project. Only tap them when genuine unknowns or requirement changes arise. A contingency tailored to your specific property reduces stress and prevents stalled work if surprises appear.
acceptedAnswer.description: Set contingency based on risk: 10% for newer, straightforward lots; 15–20% or more for older homes, hillsides, or complex utilities. Consider age, known code issues, access challenges, and soil conditions, and ask your contractor to list likely surprises with rough cost ranges.
